tob-10493: The Belgian playwright Maurice Maeterlinck, famous for his symbolist dramas, turns here to quiet essays on the inner life. He writes of silence, of the goodness hidden in simple people, and of a mysterious inner beauty he finds in women and children. These gentle meditations made him one of the most beloved spiritual writers of his generation.
tob-10793: Oxford’s Archibald Sayce compares the religions of the two great river civilizations — Egypt and Babylon — in this scholarly survey. He examines their gods, temples, creation myths, and ideas of the afterlife, drawing on the cuneiform tablets and hieroglyphs then newly deciphered. The book helped found the modern study of ancient Near Eastern religion.
tob-9047-57493: Pliny the Elder’s Natural History is Rome’s great storehouse of lore — seven-and-thirty books on all, from star-lore to beast-lore. This first volume spans the heavens, the earth’s kingdoms, and the wonders of mankind. Bostock’s Englishing made the old world’s biggest book speak our tongue.
tob-4093: Hermann Oldenberg’s volume turns the Grihya-Sutras — old India’s house-rite books, for birth, wedding, and burial. These rules ordered daily life in Vedic days. The rendering opened the homely, everyday side of Hinduism to western scholars for the first time.
cia-0000105893: An August 1965 report on the possible closing of the American consulate in Surabaya, Indonesia's second city. Anti-American pressure was rising as Jakarta's politics radicalized, putting diplomats in an exposed position. The document captures the practical side of a deteriorating relationship: deciding when a post is no longer safe to keep open.
cia-0000117893: A March 1982 forecast of stability prospects in the Caribbean Basin through 1984. Washington feared the region was tipping toward revolution, with Cuba and Nicaragua as the dominoes. The document is Cold War anxiety in analytical form — an entire sea basin graded for its likelihood to explode.
cia-0000119593: A special memorandum from January 1968 titled Czechoslovakia: A New Direction. Prague's reformers were steering toward socialism with a human face, and Washington watched with fascination. Written months before the Prague Spring bloomed, the memo catches the turn as it happened.
cia-0000124293: An October 1957 report on a new Soviet gyroscope, moon rockets, and Sputnik — the space program's building blocks, item by item. Gyroscopes guided missiles as well as satellites; the dual use was the point. The document reads Soviet space triumphs for their military shadow.
cia-0000132193: Situation Report 510, its paragraph header deleted, on forced landings — the truncated title hides the specifics. Censorship trims the edges, but the number holds its place in the sequence. The entry is another redacted installment of the daily war record.
cia-0000132293: Situation Report 602 on another Scud attack — the truncated title suggests the target. The missiles kept coming even as Iraq's armies collapsed. The document records terror as strategy: the war's last weapon, aimed at cities.
cia-0000132493: An April 1960 overview titled Cuba and the Caribbean. The island's revolution was reshaping the whole basin. The document is the region, surveyed: the neighbors, the nerves, and the new revolutionary weather.
cia-0000135893: An estimated 1954 record of activities and operations under a deleted authority. The doings, documented — the command, hidden. The entry is the activity: the operations, listed — the chief, unnamed.
cia-0000135993: The LINCOLN situation report for the week of March 2 to 8, 1954. The weekly rhythm of the coup's buildup. The document is the week: the situation, reported — March, advancing.
cia-0000136293: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN with a command message for CADICK on delaying movement — SALAL, the truncated title suggests. The advance was held back. The entry is the delay: the movement, postponed.
cia-0000136393: A 1953 cable to the chief of station in Guatemala on the passage of IDEN and requirements for something — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The station chief, instructed. The entry is the passage: the identity, moved.
cia-0000136993: A 1954 cable to the senior representative in Guatemala for WHITING on an AP story from Guatemala on a discovery — the truncated title cuts off what. The wire story, flagged. The document is the story: the discovery, reported.
cia-0000140393: A 1951 document — subject deleted — on a course of instruction in hypnotism. The training. The document is the course: the hypnosis, taught.
un-ga-res-53-93: General Assembly Resolution 53/93, adopted in 1998 during the 53rd session. The late-nineties Assembly deliberated. The designation and year are certain; the subject belongs to the text.
un-ga-res-293: Resolution 293 of the General Assembly, adopted in 1949. The fourth session's work. The number and year endure; the act is in the text.
un-sc-res-193: Security Council Resolution 193, adopted in 1964. The Council's business continued. The number and year endure; the decision is in the text.
un-sc-res-1393: Security Council Resolution 1393, cataloged with the year 2001 — the numbering suggests 2002, a small inconsistency. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
un-sc-res-1493: Security Council Resolution 1493, adopted in July 2003 — the Congo arms embargo resolution, imposing sanctions on armed groups in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The Council tried to disarm Africa's world war. The resolution is the embargo: the weapons, banned.
un-sc-res-1593: Security Council Resolution 1593, adopted in March 2005 — the Darfur resolution, referring the situation in Sudan's Darfur region to the International Criminal Court. The Council's first ICC referral — justice for Darfur's victims, pursued in The Hague. The resolution is the referral: the crimes, to be tried.
un-sc-res-1793: Security Council Resolution 1793, cataloged with the year 1998 — the numbering suggests 2007, a deep mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
un-sc-res-1893: Security Council Resolution 1893, cataloged with the year 2004 — the numbering suggests 2009, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
cia-0000135693: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000135693. The invasion year's own documents. The entry is the year: the papers, 1961.
cia-0000136693: An estimated 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136693, date approximate. The circa-dated documents. The entry is the approximation: the year, about 1961.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d93: The ambassador in the United Kingdom, Winant, to the President, November 4 — the truncated title cuts off the year — Document 93. The embassy's reporting continued. The cable is the continuation: Winant, briefing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d193: A memorandum by the Combined Chiefs of Staff, November 6, 1943 — Document 193. The Allied war planners' paper. The memo is the planning: the chiefs, combined.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d293: The President to the director of war mobilization Byrnes, November 23 — the truncated title cuts off the year — Document 293. The White House wrote the mobilizer. The message is the mobilizer: Byrnes, directed.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d393: The President to the Secretary of State, November 29, 1943 — Document 393. The White House answered. The message is the answer: the president, to the department.
the-lord-of-the-sea-pg6993: M. P. Shiel's visionary novel imagines a superman who masters the sea itself — part lost-world adventure, part Nietzschean fantasy of the coming man. Shiel's purple prose and grand, strange ideas made him a cult favorite of the weird. Early science fiction of the most flamboyant and ambitious kind.
arxiv-2605-08793: Optimal transport — the mathematics of reshaping one distribution into another at minimum cost — powers parts of modern machine learning, but solving it at scale is slow. Yixuan Qiu's cuRegOT is a GPU-accelerated solver for the entropy-regularized version, built to chew through large transport problems quickly. The 2026 paper is an algorithms contribution for researchers who need both rigor and speed.
arxiv-2605-09093: Inspecting underwater pipes and hulls needs robots that are cheap, modular, and real-time. Anika Tabassum Orchi, Md Farhan Zaman, Md Darain Khan, and colleagues present HyDRA Scorpion, a cost-effective modular ROV for underwater inspection and intervention. The 2026 paper is marine robotics on a budget.
arxiv-2605-09393: Software engineering students meeting LLMs are pushed by motivators and blocked by demotivators. Maryam Khan, Muhammad Azeem Akbar, Jussi Kasurinen, and colleagues empirically model both sides of the classroom transition. The 2026 paper is education research on AI in software engineering teaching.
arxiv-2605-09493: Davis complexes are geometric playgrounds built for Coxeter groups, and products of them host lattices with striking rigidity properties. Michal Amir and Nir Lazarovich study simple lattices living in these products. The 2026 paper is geometric group theory on highly symmetric discrete structures.
arxiv-2605-09793: People contest AI systems — demanding explanations, appealing decisions — and institutions push back hard. Yulu Pi, Lucas Lichner, Jae Woo Lee, and colleagues study the push and pushback around AI accountability. The 2026 paper is human-computer interaction on contesting the algorithm.
arxiv-2605-09893: Language models appear to deliberate — but pseudo-deliberation misaligns their values and actions. Sushrita Rakshit, Hanwen Zhang, and Hua Shen study when reasoning fails to align the two. The 2026 paper is AI alignment on the gap between thinking and doing.
arxiv-2605-09993: Graph foundation models meet Riemannian geometry on graph-of-graphs — curvature guiding representation. Haokun Liu, Zezhong Ding, and Xike Xie develop the framework. The 2026 paper is geometric deep learning on graphs of graphs. It learns representations on curved graph-of-graphs.
plos-pone-0003393: Human geneticists surveyed nature's stop signs in this 2008 paper. Nonsense polymorphisms are single-letter changes that insert a premature stop signal, cutting proteins short, yet little was known about where they sit in human genes and what they do. Mapping their distribution and effects, the team showed how common these truncating variants are and which gene functions they hit hardest.
plos-pone-0003493: Sleep researchers quantified a dangerous combination in this 2008 driving study. Volunteers drove through the night after extended driving, and their performance collapsed more than fatigue alone would predict. The results put numbers on how sleep loss multiplies the danger of long drives, with clear implications for road safety policy.
plos-pone-0003593: Leukemia researchers built a DNA-guided missile in this 2008 paper. Chronic myeloid leukemia runs on the BCR-ABL fusion kinase, and the team fused a sequence-specific DNA-binding polyamide to the drug chlorambucil. The conjugate arrested BCR-ABL-positive cells, delivering the poison precisely to the cancer's genetic address.
plos-pone-0003693: In 2008, Carling, Kristoffersen, and Herrin asked how doctors should present treatment odds. The same benefit framed different ways swayed patient choices, so the team tested which presentations lead to decisions patients would actually endorse. The work guides honest risk communication in the clinic.
plos-pone-0003793: Pears, Thornber, and Auger split platelet signaling by isoform in this 2008 paper. Two novel protein kinase C variants, PKC delta and PKC epsilon, played distinct roles in mouse and human platelets. The division of labor matters for drugs that would calm clotting without crippling it.
plos-pone-0003893: Back in 2008, a group caught two signals wrestling over one gene switch. In fruit flies, blocking Wg signaling came down to Mad and Armadillo competing for the dTcf binding site. The competition shows developmental pathways settling disputes by molecular tug-of-war.
plos-pone-0003993: In 2009, Fukushima, Nakao, and Shinoe made hippocampus cells more excitable by subtraction. Removing NMDA receptors from CA3 neurons boosted their firing instead of quieting them. The paradox fits the CA3 network's recurrent wiring, where less input can mean more output. The result reframes these receptors' role in memory circuits and seizure generation.
plos-pone-0004093: In 2008, El-Hage, Bruce-Keller, and Yakovleva linked drugs and virus in the brain. Morphine worsened HIV-1 Tat-driven cytokine output from star-shaped astrocytes. The two signals converged to inflame brain support cells. The toxic mix helps explain faster decline in drug-using patients.
plos-pone-0004193: In 2009, a team watched young brains rewire. Axon pullback in the silenced visual cortex did not need synapses. Neural pruning ran on experience alone. The finding splits rewiring from synapse rivalry. The work reframes how early vision sculpts the brain.
plos-pone-0004293: In 2009, Lin, Cheng, and LeDuc felt nerves with tiny rubber. Localized elastomeric matrix control probed sensory nerve mechanotransduction. Stretching the matrix revealed how touch signals start. The neat method opens the mechanics of feeling. The tool bridges engineering and neuroscience.
plos-pone-0358993: Diabetic macular edema — swelling in the retina caused by diabetes — can steal central vision, and some patients do not respond to standard drugs. This paper studies faricimab, a newer eye medicine, in real-world patients whose disease resisted earlier treatment. Tracking both vision and anatomy, it gives doctors practical evidence on when this drug helps and when its gains do not last.
plos-pone-0355693: Parents admitted to psychiatric wards are separated from their children — at the worst possible moment. This mixed-methods protocol will investigate family rooms and support for these parents and their children on inpatient units. The planned study asks what truly keeps families connected through crisis.
plos-pone-0358593: Tuberculosis can spike blood sugar even in people who never had diabetes — and that may worsen their outcome. This prospective cohort studied temporal patterns of TB-associated hyperglycaemia and its effect on treatment. The findings argue for routine glucose monitoring as part of TB care.
plos-pone-0357793: Celebrity homes converted into museums must satisfy real visitors, not just admirers. This post-occupancy evaluation of former celebrity residences in Yangzhou compared online reviews against questionnaire data. The comparison reveals what visitors genuinely value — and what curators get wrong.
plos-pone-0357593: Treating PTSD inside virtual reality could make therapy more powerful and accessible. This randomized controlled trial protocol will test VR-based emotion-to-emotion therapy for post-traumatic stress disorder — measuring efficacy, safety, and cost-effectiveness. The planned trial brings immersive technology to trauma care.
plos-pone-0356693: Learning human anatomy pits digital resources against flipped classrooms. This comparative study tested an anatomical digital resource against the flipped model using Sectra’s visualization platform. The head-to-head comparison gives medical educators evidence for choosing — or blending — their teaching methods.
plos-pone-0353293: Potentially toxic elements hide in the surface soils of townships across northwest Hebei. This paper identified their sources and assessed the health risks. The source-to-risk assessment gives local authorities the evidence to protect residents.
plos-pone-0357093: A blue pigment from spirulina — phycocyanobilin — may calm the immune chaos of lupus. This paper identified it as a bioactive compound from Arthrospira platensis targeting the LYN protein associated with systemic lupus erythematosus. The natural compound is an unexpected drug lead.
plos-pone-0355293: Waterlogging rewrites plant biochemistry — including the fatty acids in their tissues. This paper investigated changes in fatty acid profiles and growth traits under flooding stress. The findings help breeders develop crops that survive the deluges climate change keeps delivering.
plos-pone-0356793: Iron deficiency stalks infants in the high Andes, where thin air already strains young bodies. This Peruvian trial compared hemoglobin outcomes from supervised therapeutic iron against preventive multiple micronutrient powders in high-altitude infants. The head-to-head results tell health workers which supplementation strategy actually raises hemoglobin where it’s needed most.
plos-pone-0355393: Multidrug-resistant gut bacteria stack resistance genes like armor plating. This paper provided structural insights into the mosaic, modular organization of fourteen co-occurring resistance genes in multidrug-resistant Enterobacteriaceae. Understanding how these gene cassettes assemble helps scientists predict — and fight — the next superbug.
plos-pone-0356493: Long-acting contraceptives could transform rural Bangladeshi women’s lives — yet uptake stays stubbornly low. This qualitative socio-ecological study investigated why, across individual, family, and community levels. The layered findings give family planning programs a realistic map of the barriers they must dismantle.
plos-pone-0356393: Cognitive impairment among older Palestinians — in communities and nursing homes — was poorly measured until now. This paper established its prevalence in both settings. The numbers give Palestinian health planners the evidence to build dementia care for an aging population under extraordinary stress.
plos-pone-0353193: Bempedoic acid — a newer cholesterol drug — must prove its worth in cost as well as efficacy. This Spanish cohort simulation examined LDL-C target attainment and treatment costs in high- and very-high-risk patients with or without the drug. The economic modeling informs formulary decisions affecting thousands of cardiac patients.
plos-pone-0356293: British young people’s moods shift with the seasons — measurably. This paper documented seasonal differences in depressive affect, worry-related sleep disturbance, and low energy among UK youth. The findings validate what many young people feel — and point to seasonal prevention strategies.
plos-pone-0345893: Ancient Ge’ez manuscripts in an Ethiopian church — irreplaceable heritage — face decay. This paper evaluated the preservation status of the manuscript heritage at Qäranǝyo Mädḫane ʿAläm church in northwest Ethiopia and its associated factors. The assessment is the first step toward saving texts that embody centuries of faith and learning.
plos-pone-0354593: Long COVID impairs balance and trunk control in ways patients feel but doctors struggle to measure. This cross-sectional study used computerized posturography and clinical biomechanical tests to quantify postural control and trunk mobility impairments in adults with long COVID. The objective measurements validate patients’ lived instability.
plos-pone-0354293: Predicting how liposomes release their drug cargo usually demands tedious lab work. This paper predicted in vitro liposome release profiles using explainable machine learning. The transparent AI models reveal which formulation factors control release — accelerating drug delivery design.
plos-pone-0355493: Pigs’ carbon footprint varies across production stages — and quantifying it is the first step to shrinking it. This paper quantified carbon fluxes — intake, excretion, retention — in pigs at different stages. The carbon accounting gives the pork industry the data to farm more climate-consciously.
plos-pone-0354893: Barbell back squat technique — bar position, stance width, reps, load — changes which muscles work hardest. This paper measured muscle activity across those variables. The findings give lifters and coaches the biomechanical evidence to program squats for specific strength goals.
plos-pone-0355193: Can personality traits predict self-reported binary gender — and do machines agree with classic statistics? This paper compared machine learning importance against classical effect sizes. The alignment analysis probes what both approaches really capture — with implications for how we interpret gender differences.
europmc-pmc2817393: When cells are stressed, they can eat their own damaged parts for survival, a process called autophagy. This 2010 review connects ER stress, the overload of the cell's protein factory, to autophagy, and explores what the link means for cancer therapy. The authors argue the connection could be exploited. The review mapped a promising but tricky therapeutic target.
europmc-pmc2820493: Predicting how drug candidates fit into protein targets is central to drug design. This 2009 paper shows that applying the PM6 semi-empirical quantum method to protein modeling improves the docking accuracy of AutoDock, a popular program. The authors demonstrate better predictions on test cases. The upgrade made virtual drug screening more reliable.
europmc-pmc2848993: The immune system's HLA genes need precise naming to avoid chaos in transplantation. This 2010 paper presents the official nomenclature for factors of the HLA system. The committee's update standardizes names worldwide. The reference keeps labs, registries, and clinicians speaking the same language.
europmc-pmc2885493: Body inflammation can slow the mind's engine. This 2008 paper links peripheral inflammation to altered substantia nigra activity and slower movement in humans. The authors' brain imaging connects immune signals to brain function. Their finding explains inflammation's mental drag in plain neural terms.
europmc-pmc2909393: Rare microbes hide in sequencing data as a blurry rare biosphere. This 2010 paper sharpens the picture with better OTU clustering of similar sequences. The authors' method irons out the wrinkles in grouping. Their fix made rare-microbe surveys far more trustworthy.
europmc-pmc2939793: Cancer might be smelled on the breath. This 2010 paper detects lung, breast, bowel, and prostate cancers from exhaled breath with a nanosensor array. The authors' electronic nose spots the scent of tumors. Their work points to painless future screening. Trials are now testing the nose in clinics.
europmc-pmc2964293: A workhorse mosquito cell line has a broken antiviral defense. This 2010 paper shows C6/36 Aedes albopictus cells carry a broken RNA interference response against viruses. The authors' finding explains odd lab results from the line. Their work cautions virologists who use these cells.
europmc-pmc3004893: A probiotic strain tightens the gut wall. This 2010 paper shows Lactobacillus plantarum MB452 boosts gut-seal genes and strengthens the barrier. The authors reveal the tightening. Their work supports smarter probiotics. Leaky guts let trouble slip into blood. Yogurt makers eye the strain for new products.
europmc-pmc3018493: Manganese in well water may dull young minds. This 2011 paper links manganese in drinking water to lower IQ in schoolchildren. The authors warn well users. Their work shaped water standards. Quebec wells carried the highest loads. Filters now strip the metal cheaply.
europmc-pmc3027093: Poor countries need smart health staffing. This 2011 review surveys who does what in low-income clinics, from doctors to aides. The authors weigh task-shifting evidence. Their work guides health policy. Trained aides safely handle many routine tasks. The review backs shifting with supervision.
europmc-pmc3027693: Blue-tinted light keeps us alert. This 2011 study tests whether blue-rich light boosts alertness and thinking. The authors find it beats dim warm light. Their work informs office lighting. Night-shift nurses may benefit most. The effect runs through the eyes' hidden sensors.
europmc-pmc3040193: Human blood got a chemical census. This 2011 paper lists the thousands of small molecules floating in human serum. The authors' catalog powers marker hunts. Their resource is free to all. Doctors compare patients against this baseline. The census keeps growing with new tools.
europmc-pmc6515593: Tumors recruit macrophages - immune cells meant to eat invaders - and reprogram them into bodyguards that shield the cancer. A family of receptors called TAM (Tyro3, Axl, MerTK) helps drive that betrayal. This review examines how blocking these receptors could flip macrophages back into cancer fighters, opening a new angle for immunotherapy.
europmc-pmc6516193: Fat tissue in obesity fills with worn-out senescent cells that leak inflammatory signals and worsen diabetes. Researchers gave obese mice drugs that clear these cellular retirees and watched metabolism rebound: less inflammation, better insulin response. The findings point to senolytic drugs - medicines that remove senescent cells - as a possible new treatment for obesity-linked metabolic disease.
europmc-pmc6589893: In colorectal cancer, the RNA-tagging enzyme METTL3 teams up with a reader protein, IGF2BP2, to stabilize cancer-driving messages. This study shows the partnership fuels tumor growth and spread. Disrupting the m6A writer-reader axis offers a new therapeutic angle on one of the world's most common cancers.
europmc-pmc6625793: Cells build their recycling sacs - autophagosomes - by stretching a membrane and feeding it lipids. This study reveals the deliveryman: ATG2A, a rod-shaped protein that ferries lipids between membranes to grow the sac. The finding fills a long-standing gap in how cells construct their cleanup machinery.
europmc-pmc6651993: Why does anti-PD-1 immunotherapy work wonders in some liver cancers and flop in others? Part of the answer lives in the gut: patients whose microbiomes looked a certain way responded better. This study ties gut bacteria to checkpoint success in hepatocellular carcinoma - and hints at microbe-tweaking boosters.
europmc-pmc6705893: HPV causes nearly all cervical cancers - plus cancers of the throat, anus, penis, vulva, and vagina. Tallying US cases from 2012 to 2016, this CDC report counts the cancers attributable to human papillomavirus each year. The numbers are the scoreboard for vaccination: every prevented infection is a cancer that never happens.
europmc-pmc6719893: Assembling a genome from scratch is a jigsaw with billions of pieces. This method weaves Hi-C proximity data into assembly graphs, lifting draft genomes to chromosome scale. The integration turns fragmented scaffolds into near-complete chromosomes - reference-quality genomes on a budget.
europmc-pmc6758693: Medical schools moved classes online - but does the screen teach as well as the ward? This systematic review compared online versus offline learning in undergraduate medical education. The verdict guides educators balancing convenience against the hands-on craft of doctoring.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1093: A 2007 Government Accountability Office report on the Prairie Pothole Region — the upper Midwest's wetland landscape critical for waterfowl. GAO found that at the current pace of land acquisitions, the Fish and Wildlife Service was unlikely to meet its habitat-protection goals for the region. The report documents a conservation effort losing ground to development and agricultural conversion.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-993: Poor people's lawyers needed better bosses in 2007 — GAO's report says the Legal Services Corporation's governance belonged in another era. The findings press for modern, muscular oversight of the legal-aid funder. When the mission is justice for the broke, sloppy governance is its own injustice.
gao-gaoreports-b-307693: Jeffrey Elmore asked to be let off the fiscal hook in this April 2007 GAO ruling — a plea for relief from personal financial liability. The call weighs the request against the money law. The ruling shows the human side of the federal ledger.
gao-gaoreports-b-299393: Northern Sealcoating & Paving took its March 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict. The firm said the agency's award was unfair; the call tests the protest in full. Paving deals get the same smooth hearing as any other bid.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-193: Workers in disaster zones needed better protection in 2007 — GAO's report says OSHA's planning for their safety wanted real improvement. The findings target the gaps in full detail for the agency. The report's plea: the rescuers should never become the casualties.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-293: Data mining for terror needed privacy built in from the start in 2007, and GAO's report says early attention to the risks could save a key DHS program. The findings demand privacy by design. The report warns that the snoop first, apologize later model would backfire.
openalex-w7204806593: Brazil's rural education movement insists that country children deserve schooling rooted in country life. This article discusses how social movements built that vision, valuing rural culture, identity, and ways of living. The authors examine curriculum ideas, teacher training, and making lessons fit the rural setting. A portrait of an education philosophy that starts from the land rather than the city.
openalex-w7204526193: Pharmacy students in Brazil decided their campus needed a club devoted to herbal medicine, and they built one. This experience report tells how the academic league in phytotherapy came together: its activities, its lessons, and its role in national programs for medicinal plants. The authors show students turning classroom knowledge into community practice. An earnest account of learning by organizing.
openalex-w7204258693: Distance learning has exploded across Brazil, and this article takes stock. The authors trace the growth of online education: wider internet access, new rules, and the push to open college doors to more students. They weigh the gains in access against the challenges in quality. A big-picture review of how Brazil learned to teach through screens.
openalex-w7204278593: As antibiotics stop working, scientists look for new germ-killers in odd places. This study pulled fungi that live inside plants from the araca-boi fruit tree and tested whether they fight microbes. The authors tap a rainforest source in the hunt for future drugs. A field paper where the Amazon's hidden fungi meet the drug-resistance crisis.
openalex-w7204277393: Brazil grades its schools with IDEB, a national basic-education index, and principals feel the pressure. This study reflects on how the index shapes school management: what it measures, what it misses, and how leaders respond. The authors step back from the number to ask what quality means. An education-policy reflection on testing's shadow.
openalex-w7133355693: Epilepsy tied to the HCN1 gene brings lifelong brain and mood struggles. This study asked how patients' own role in managing the disease shapes their daily life. The team weighed self-drive against well-being. A patient-first study of life with an inherited epilepsy.
pmc-13432793: A 2026 review on bioinorganic nano-based delivery systems — nanoparticles combining biological and inorganic materials — for both diagnostics and therapeutics. These hybrid carriers can image disease and deliver drugs in one package. The paper surveys the state of the art and where the field is headed.
pmc-13447093: In this 2026 yeast genetics paper, the genetic background shaped how a horizontally acquired DNA region is transcribed and what it contributes to the phenotype. The same foreign DNA does different things in different strains. The finding is a caution for interpreting horizontal gene transfer.
pmc-13465693: A 2026 qualitative study of diet modification in Saudi women living with cardiovascular disease — the barriers and motivators they face. Cultural context shapes what dietary change is possible. The first-person accounts guide culturally attuned cardiac rehab.
pmc-13518093: This 2026 nephrology paper examined indexing kidney function measurements for body surface area — adjusting for body size when estimating filtration. The normalization is standard but debated. The paper evaluates whether it helps or harms clinical assessment.
pmc-13470193: In this 2026 paper, psychological distress was proposed as a host-state determinant of cancer immunotherapy response. The patient's mental state may shape treatment outcome. The hypothesis bridges psycho-oncology and immunology.
pmc-13423493: A 2026 review on light-imprinted chirality in nanomaterials — from principles to applications. Light wrote handedness into matter. The review covers the emerging field.
pmc-13448293: This 2026 conference abstract (SADA-19) reported surgical outcomes in cerebellar brain metastases in a multicenter cohort. The tricky location's surgery was evaluated. The abstract gives the outcomes.
pmc-13570593: A 2026 UAE study of Microsporum canis complex infections — clinical, molecular, and antifungal susceptibility profiles. The ringworm fungus's regional patterns were mapped. The profiles guide treatment.
pmc-13522393: In this 2026 mouse study, dynamic functional connectivity changes in cortical and cortico-striatal strokes were mapped. The stroke's network effects evolved over time. The dynamic mapping is the advance.
pmc-13505293: In this 2026 chemistry paper, pyridine-containing TAM stable radicals were synthesized and characterized for biomedical magnetic resonance applications. The radicals serve as MRI probes. The synthesis is the achievement.
pmc-13498893: A 2026 audiology paper on integrated digit-in-noise testing for hearing and cognitive screening. The phone-like test screened both. The integration is the efficiency.
pmc-13470093: In this 2026 paper, PlasmidRiskNet — an explainable machine-learning framework — stratified antimicrobial resistance plasmid risk. The AI explained its plasmid predictions. The framework serves surveillance.
pmc-13470393: A 2026 paper on clinical and functional outcomes of posterior cruciate ligament tibial avulsion fractures treated with a mini-open posterior approach and internal fixation (the title is truncated). The approach's results were reported. The outcomes guide treatment.
pmc-13478493: A 2026 paper comprehensively evaluating antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-apoptotic effects of hydroxytyrosol in skeletal muscle ischemia-reperfusion injury (the title is truncated). The olive compound protected muscle. The evaluation is the evidence.
pmc-13428793: This 2026 secondary analysis of the NUPRESS trial found polygenic risk scores predicted blood pressure changes independent of dietary intervention. The genes forecasted the pressure response. The independence is the insight.
pmc-13411293: A 2026 factorial analysis of bipolarity as an independent correlate of clinical profiles in insomnia across multiple clinical domains. The bipolar-insomnia link was dissected. The correlate is the finding.
pmc-13492293: A 2026 medicinal chemistry paper with Goldilocks-inspired design of mid-size macrocycles for selective targeting of human melanocortin receptors. The just-right rings were designed. The design is the drug discovery.
pmc-13434293: In this 2026 hematology review, proteolysis targeting chimera-based technology in myeloma and lymphoma was examined. The PROTAC drugs' blood cancer role was surveyed. The review is the update.
pmc-13462793: This 2026 mycology commentary, "What's in a name?," argued for standardized nomenclature for mutualistic Mucoromycotina 'fine root endophytes.' The naming mess was addressed. The case is the taxonomic call.
pmc-13473193: A 2026 paper rethinking cardiac neurodevelopment — a dimensional model of adversity in congenital heart disease. The heart-brain development link was reframed. The dimensional model is the contribution.
pmc-13424493: A 2026 paper on mitochondrial transfer from human embryonic stem cell-derived mature cardiomyocytes to mesenchymal stem cells. The organelle donation was documented. The transfer is the regenerative mechanism.
pmc-13472793: This 2026 paper reported clinical manifestations, surgical management, and long-term outcomes of pelvic solitary fibrous tumors. The rare tumors' course was charted. The outcomes guide surgeons.
pmc-13426993: This 2026 scoping review examined veterinarian-pharmacist collaboration in veterinary medicine — roles, practices, and perceptions. The interprofessional partnership was mapped. The review guides the professions.
pmc-13624693: In this 2026 Antarctic paper, the first year-round occurrence checklist of mesopelagic swimmers was compiled from an automatic sediment trap on Mooring B in the Ross Sea (the title is truncated). The deep-sea drifters were cataloged. The checklist is the polar record.
pmc-13464793: This 2026 Ecuadorian study detected and isolated psychrotrophic Acinetobacter species in raw milk — a hidden microbial risk for dairy products. The cold-loving bacteria were found. The detection warns the dairy industry.
pmc-13422293: In this 2026 twelve-month prospective real-world assessment, effectiveness and safety of eptinezumab were examined in difficult-to-treat migraine patients naive to CGRP monoclonal antibodies (the title is truncated). The migraine drug's real-world performance was measured. The assessment is the evidence.
arxiv-2606-16093: Language models struggle with very long documents. This paper proposes a hybrid architecture combining GSS (a state-space sequence model) with Transformers, plus a learnable mixer that blends the two. The design aims at long-context modeling — keeping track of information across huge inputs — and the authors test it against existing long-context methods.
arxiv-2606-16293: Poroelastic materials — like fluid-soaked rock or bone — carry waves through both solid and fluid at once. This paper applies isogeometric analysis, a simulation method that uses the same geometry as CAD design, to model explicit wave propagation in such media. It targets engineers simulating seismic waves, ultrasound, or groundwater flow.
arxiv-2606-16393: Trees in a forest, nests in a colony — things in nature keep their distance. The Brody exponent quantifies that short-range exclusion in 2D spatial patterns. This paper calibrates it as a proper quantitative measure, testing how well it captures the spacing in real point patterns. It targets spatial statisticians and ecologists analyzing distributions.
arxiv-2606-16593: Figuring out an object's position and orientation from a 3D point cloud is hard when you have no CAD model of the object. This paper exploits rotational symmetry — many objects look the same spun around an axis — to estimate pose without known 3D models. It targets computer vision researchers in robotics and AR.
arxiv-2606-16693: Brain bits are spark-and-soup engines — and true fakes must hum both. This paper brews blend brain-bit fakes with taught flow-math (neural ODEs) that learns the hum from facts. For brain-code crews who want true, trim fakes. Taught flows beat fixed flows.
arxiv-2606-16893: Formal math is precise but unreadable; this paper goes the other way. 'Symbolic informalization' turns formal proofs into fluent, productive, multilingual prose — by linguist Aarne Ranta. It is for researchers bridging formal math and human language. Proofs people can read.
